judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short agreement-to-purchase whose quantum is "an amount set forth on the Mortgage Loan Schedule" rather than a stated figure.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Schedule is said to be attached as Exhibit B, but Exhibit B reads "Provided Upon Request", so the quantity sold is not ascertainable within the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A delivery deadline with a proviso excusing delays caused by the Purchaser, qualified only by "a reasonable period of time".
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 9(i) also requires a complete Mortgage Loan Schedule as a closing condition, which fits this two-Business-Day requirement.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The price formula is complete in form but its key multiplier, the Purchase Price Percentage, is defined only by reference to an external Letter Agreement; interest passes from the Closing Date while principal passes from the Cut-off Date.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Closing Date (May 31, 2007) precedes the Cut-off Date (June 1, 2007), so a formula keyed to Cut-off Date balances and post-Cut-off principal cannot be applied straightforwardly at closing.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clear examination mechanics with an express statement that failure to examine does not affect repurchase rights.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It locates the Custodian on "the Mortgage Loan Schedule attached as Exhibit B", while Section 7 places the Schedule at Exhibit C — inconsistent exhibit references for the same document.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Operative conveyance language is clear; the two carve-outs (Servicing Rights and the Group 1 exception) are expressly stated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Exhibit C lists Prior Purchase Agreements only for non-Group 1 originators, and Subsection 8.02 gives the Purchaser the Originators' warranties "as described in Subsection 6.01", so what the Purchaser received for Group 1 loans has to be pieced together.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The passage ends mid-sentence ("and a asa a sale of assets 0 on the"), and it says record title stays in the Seller's name while ownership "shall be vested solely in the Purchaser" — two statements about title in one paragraph.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It reinforces the sale characterisation also stated in Section 17, but Section 13's grant of a security interest by the Seller in the same loans pulls the other way.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clear three-step mechanic: certifications, authorisation to hold, then fees.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It puts custodial fees on the Purchaser after closing, while Section 11 allocates "all other costs and expenses incurred in connection with the transfer and delivery" between the parties — compatible but requiring reconciliation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Specific MERS designation obligations; "promptly following the Closing Date" is the only soft term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the MERS Designated Mortgage Loan, Investor and Interim Funder definitions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It states the loans are sold "servicing retained" and then describes servicing being transferred to Saxon, and it locates the Mortgage Loan Schedule at "Exhibit C".
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 5 and the Mortgage Loan Schedule definition place the Schedule at Exhibit B and Exhibit C holds the Prior Purchase and Servicing Agreements, so the exhibit references conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A long but conventional due-organisation and authority representation with standard enforceability qualifiers.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Exhibit D section 2(g), which repeats it almost verbatim for the Assignor.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The sentence contains a duplicated verb — "No consent ... is required for the transactions ... having jurisdiction over the Seller is required" — so the syntax collapses.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Exhibit D section 2(h) reproduces the identical broken sentence, showing it was copied rather than negotiated.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line ordinary-course representation with a minor number disagreement ("transactions ... are").
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the sale-treatment representation in 8.01(g) and Section 17.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Notably narrow: the no-conflicts representation is limited to the Seller's charter or by-laws and says nothing about law or other contracts.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The principal agreement's Sections 7(c) and 9(c) cover laws and orders as well, so the two instruments give different comfort on the same point.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard no-litigation representation limited to proceedings attacking the agreement.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Mirrored in Exhibit D section 2(i); no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A belief-based representation phrased as a double negative ("does not believe, nor does it have any reason or cause to believe, that it cannot perform"), so what is actually warranted is elusive.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Nothing else in the agreement builds on this representation, though it is caught by the repurchase machinery in Subsection 8.02 via Subsections 8.01 and 8.02.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Drafted as a covenant ("shall treat") within a representations subsection, but its content is unambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Subsection 6.02 and Section 17's true-sale intention.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The core repurchase machinery: a 120-day window running from the earlier of discovery or notice, "best efforts promptly to cure", a deeming rule for clauses (N),(O),(R),(W),(Y), the Purchaser's option, and a sole-remedies clause — several of these phrases are the classic battlegrounds.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is keyed to breach of a "Representation and Warranty", a term defined as the Originators' warranties, while the Seller's own warranties sit on Exhibit F, and its 180-day substitution limit interacts with Section 12's Reconstitution and Subsection 8.03.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It says "a Mortgage Loan suffers a FPD" although FPD is defined as contractual provisions, and the second sentence packs two very different triggers into a single conditional with hard-coded 2007 dates.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The first trigger depends on breach of clause (D) of Part B of Exhibit F, and the FPD provisions themselves live in the Prior Purchase Agreements, which for Group 1 loans were not assigned under Subsection 6.01.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The conditions list is typographically scrambled — items (iv) and (v) appear before the text they head — and it repeatedly speaks of "each Closing Date" although only one Closing Date is defined.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 10 likewise refers to documents "for each Closing Date" and marks this Agreement as delivered "only for the initial Closing Date", suggesting a multi-closing template imperfectly adapted to a single closing.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The enumeration breaks down after "1.", leaving four further documents unnumbered, and the parenthetical "(to be executed and delivered only for the initial Closing Date)" presupposes multiple closings.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It requires delivery of the Letter Agreement, which is between Morgan Stanley & Co. and Bear Stearns & Co. rather than the parties, and of custodian certifications under Subsection 6.03.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A clear two-sided cost allocation with a residual sweep to the Purchaser ("All other costs and expenses").
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 24 also puts recordation at the Seller's expense and Subsection 6.03 puts custodial fees on the Purchaser, so the allocations line up.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Long, with several soft standards ("cooperate fully", "reasonable best efforts", "reasonably acceptable") and an indemnity whose clause (B) is qualified by a bespoke construction proviso.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It limits the Purchaser to one Reconstitution while Section 18 limits the Purchaser to "three (3) assignments or transfers with respect to the Mortgage Loans and this Agreement as described in Section 12" — a direct numerical conflict about the same activity.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It grants a lien and continuing security interest in loans the Seller has just sold, and says the Seller "shall hold such Mortgage Loans in custody", which is hard to square with an outright conveyance.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Subsection 6.02 and Section 17 both insist the transaction is a sale and not a pledge, so this grant has to be read as a fallback rather than as an operative retained interest.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Notices are "deemed to have been duly given if mailed" but, "if by other means, when received", and the closing sentence then makes everything effective on delivery — three receipt rules that do not sit together.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The principal agreement's Section 18 adopts a purely receipt-based rule with business-hours qualifications, so the two instruments differ on when notice bites — significant given the notice-triggered repurchase clocks.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Comprehensive severability with a good-faith renegotiation obligation; "nearly as possible the same" is loose but aspirational.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The principal agreement's Section 22 states a narrower rule, but they govern different instruments.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Boilerplate counterparts clause; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the separately-executed signature pages.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A tax-characterisation clause with a grantor-trust fallback; its intent is plainly stated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Subsection 6.02 and 8.01(g), though Section 13's security interest grant is the usual counterweight.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Free assignability for the Purchaser but capped at "three (3) assignments or transfers", a limit whose relationship to the assignment right is not explained.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: That three-transfer cap is expressed to be "as described in Section 12", yet Section 12 limits the Purchaser to one Reconstitution — the two numbers cannot both govern.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard no-oral-waiver clause; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Mirrored in Exhibit D section 4; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One line incorporating the exhibits; unambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Exhibit B is not reproduced ("Provided Upon Request"), so incorporation makes an unattached schedule part of the contract.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard interpretive rules; limb (f) expressly makes "include" non-limiting, which cuts against ejusdem generis arguments elsewhere.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It applies only to this annexed agreement, and the principal agreement contains no equivalent, so the two documents are construed by different rules.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An evidentiary reproduction clause; broad but plainly worded.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Nothing else in the agreement addresses document reproduction; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short further-assurances covenant bounded by "reasonable and appropriate".
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Overlaps Section 12's cooperation obligations without contradicting them.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Recording is required where "necessary under applicable law or requested by the Purchaser at its sole option", which is definite, though "subject to recordation" is an odd formulation for an obligation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Exhibit A-1(e) states a third trigger — recording where "commonly required by private institutional mortgage investors in the area" — which this section omits.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The first carve-out is broken: "so long as such promotional material either is sent to the mortgagors for all of the mortgages in the servicing portfolio" offers an "either" with no alternative, so the permitted conduct cannot be delimited.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The final paragraph excludes general-public promotions from "solicitation", overlapping the same carve-out and leaving two differently-worded safe harbours for similar conduct.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conventional jury-waiver in capitals; unambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 27's forum selection; the principal agreement has no jury waiver, but they are separate instruments.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Detailed choice of law, exclusive jurisdiction and service provisions; each limb is clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Exhibit D section 3 and with the principal agreement's New York choice of law.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A privacy covenant tied to a named statute; "policies, procedures, and safeguards designed to protect" is a standard formulation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Nothing else addresses borrower privacy; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A clear lead-in identifying the delivery obligation and the inspecting parties, including "any prospective Purchaser".
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It refers delivery to "Section 6" generally, whereas the Mortgage Loan Documents definition points specifically to Subsection 6.03; a minor looseness.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The required endorsement is quoted with the payee left blank — "Pay to the order of , Without recourse" — and the allonge permission depends on the Seller advising the Purchaser what state law allows.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The principal agreement's Section 4(b) governs delivery of Mortgage Notes to the Trustee with lost-note alternatives, so endorsement form matters across both instruments.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One line permitting an original or imaged copy; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the imaged-copy approach used throughout Exhibit A-1.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Long but carefully structured around three named causes of non-delivery, each with its own certification route; "original or an imaged copy of the original" as equivalents is the only loose point.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The principal agreement's Section 4(b) requires originals or certified true copies delivered to the Trustee, a stricter regime than imaged copies, so the two delivery standards differ.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Requires originals "with evidence of recording thereon" for all such agreements, without the imaged-copy fallback allowed elsewhere.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Exhibit F clause (Q) warrants that modifications have been recorded only "if necessary to protect the interests of the Purchaser", a softer standard than this absolute requirement.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Recording is required where "commonly required by private institutional mortgage investors in the area where the Mortgaged Property is located", a trade-practice standard, and the MERS carve-out is mis-numbered in the singular.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 24 states the recording trigger differently (necessary under law or requested by the Purchaser), and the Assignment of Mortgage definition requires the instrument to be "in blank" in all cases.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It requires a chain of assignment "from the Seller to the Last Endorsee", which reverses the direction of title — intervening assignments run to, not from, the Seller.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Exhibit A-1(a) defines the Last Endorsee as the party endorsing to the Purchaser, so this chain description cannot be reconciled with the endorsement regime.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Allows an imaged copy of the title policy or, if unavailable, a certified copy of the binder or commitment; clear alternatives.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Exhibit F clause (G) warrants an actual ALTA or CLTA policy, so a binder-only file would sit awkwardly with that warranty.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One line; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Matches the security-agreement limb of Exhibit F clause (E).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The sub-list is mis-numbered ("the (i) the Co-op Lease") and it calls for imaged copies of items — a stock certificate and undated stock power executed in blank — that only work as originals.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Security Agreement and Co-op UCC Filing definitions treat these as perfection documents, which imaged copies cannot achieve.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short catch-all for powers of attorney; definite in its requirement of a certified copy.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Sections 7(d) and 9(d) of the principal agreement contemplate unrecorded powers of attorney, consistent with this item.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The list is mis-lettered (item (l) appears as "(i)") and item (j) closes with "etc.", an open-ended catch-all after specific examples.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It limits contents to items "in the possession of the applicable Seller" while the Mortgage File definition says "in the possession of the applicable Servicer", a straight inconsistency about whose files are captured.
